question: Does dimensionality reduction always make data easier to use for prediction?
direct_answer: No; it can help, but it can also remove predictive information.
expanded_answer: Dimensionality reduction may improve efficiency, reduce noise, or help with generalization, but it is not guaranteed to preserve the information needed for a specific target. Methods like PCA preserve variance, not necessarily task-relevant signal, so some prediction problems may get worse after reduction.
key_points: It may help or hurt prediction
common_wrong_ideas: Fewer dimensions always means better models
High-variance directions are always the most predictive
